record.title: Diameter conjecture for McKay graphs of finite simple groups
record.statement:
For a finite group $G$, let ${\rm Irr}(G)$ denote its irreducible characters. For a complex character $\alpha$ of $G$, the **McKay graph** $\mathcal{M}(G,\alpha)$ is the directed graph with vertex set ${\rm Irr}(G)$, with an edge from $\chi_1$ to $\chi_2$ exactly when $\chi_2$ is a constituent of $\alpha\chi_1$. Write $\mathsf{diam}\mathcal{M}(G,\alpha)$ for its diameter.

**Diameter conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $C$ such that for any finite non-abelian simple group $G$, and any nontrivial irreducible character $\alpha$ of $G$,

$$
\mathsf{diam}\mathcal{M}(G,\alpha) \le C\frac{\log |G|}{\log \alpha(1)}.
$$

The conjecture seeks an upper bound for McKay-graph diameters of the same logarithmic order as the natural lower bounds in terms of $|G|$ and the degree $\alpha(1)$. Its status is not established by the supplied text.
record.source_name: Martin W. Liebeck, Aner Shalev and Pham Huu Tiep, “On the diameters of McKay graphs for finite simple groups”, arXiv:1911.13284 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.13284

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2019).

record.title: The linear-logarithmic induced-path conjecture for triangle-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a triangle-free graph with chromatic number $\chi$. An **induced path** is a path whose vertices induce exactly the edges of the path.

**Linear-logarithmic induced-path conjecture.** There is some constant $c>0$ such that every triangle-free graph of chromatic number $\chi$ contains an induced path of length at least $c\chi\log\chi$.

This is a quantitative strengthening of the known fact that triangle-free graphs of chromatic number $\chi$ contain induced paths of length at least $\chi$. The supplied status evidence concerns a different Gyárfás conjecture, so this conjecture is retained as open.
record.source_name: N. R. Aravind, Stijn Cambie, Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Rémi de Joannis de Verclos, Ross J. Kang and Viresh Patel, “Structure and colour in triangle-free graphs”, arXiv:1912.13328 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.13328

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

record.title: Bipartite random friends-and-strangers graph component conjecture
record.statement: Let $r$ be a positive integer, let $p\in[0,1]$, and let $X$ and $Y$ be independently chosen random graphs from $\mathcal G(K_{r,r},p)$, where $K_{r,r}$ is the complete bipartite graph with parts of size $r$. Write $\operatorname{\mathsf{FS}}(X,Y)$ for their friends-and-strangers graph. **Bipartite component conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that if $p\geq Cr^{-1/2}$, then $\operatorname{\mathsf{FS}}(X,Y)$ has exactly $2$ connected components with high probability. This conjecture concerns the typical number of components in the bipartite random setting and would sharpen the paper’s estimates; its resolution is not supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Noga Alon, Colin Defant and Noah Kravitz, “Typical and Extremal Aspects of Friends-and-Strangers Graphs”, arXiv:2009.07840 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.07840

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2020).

record.title: The short-partition model conjecture for prime gaps
record.statement: Let $p_n$ be the $n$th prime, let $\mathcal P$ denote the set of partitions, and let $\widehat{N}$ be the supernorm map. A partition has no $1$'s when none of its parts equals $1$, and its length is its number of parts. **Short-partition model conjecture for prime gaps.** For $n\geq 1$, the odd numbers in the interval $[p_n,p_{n+1})$ can be modeled by the values of $\widehat{N}$ on partitions of norm $n$ having no part equal to $1$ and length exactly one or two. This is a provisional heuristic based on simplifying postulates: longer partitions are assumed to contribute negligibly to the prime-gap estimate, and the relevant length-one and length-two partitions are expected to account for most odd values in the gap. It is explicitly a model rather than an established theorem, and no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Madeline Locus Dawsey, Matthew Just and Robert Schneider, “A "supernormal" partition statistic”, arXiv:2107.14284 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.14284

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

record.title: Dahlberg–Shepherd conjecture on the maximum degree of e-positive trees
record.statement:
A tree is a connected acyclic graph. A tree is **$e$-positive** when the expansion of its chromatic symmetric function in the elementary symmetric-function basis has only nonnegative coefficients.

**Dahlberg–Shepherd conjecture.** Any tree with a vertex of degree at least $4$ is not $e$-positive.

The source notes that every $n$-vertex $e$-positive tree has degree at most $\log_2 n$, and that positivity has been proved impossible when a vertex has degree at least $6$. Thus the degree-$4$ and degree-$5$ cases remain relevant to the conjecture.
record.source_name: David G. L. Wang and Monica M. Y. Wang, “The e-positivity and Schur positivity of the chromatic symmetric functions of some trees”, arXiv:2112.06619 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.06619

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2021). “conjectured the existence of an $n$-vertex Schur positive tree of maximum degree $\floor{n/2}$, which is disproved by with a counterexample.”

record.title: Higher-dimensional connectivity and chromatic number conjecture for random distance graphs on spheres
record.statement:
Let $d\geq1$ and let $\alpha$ be an angular parameter. For a random $\varepsilon$-distance graph on the sphere, write $\mathcal{N}(\distgraph[n,\varepsilon])$ for its neighborhood complex, and let $\operatorname{conn}$ denote connectivity. Assume there is a constant $\mathcal{C}_d$ as in the random-net model. **Higher-dimensional connectivity and chromatic number conjecture.** There exists a constant $\lambda_d<\pi$ such that, whenever

$$
\lambda_d\leq\alpha\leq\pi,\qquad \varepsilon\geq\mathcal{C}_d(\log n/n)^{1/d},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \varepsilon\to0,
$$

a.a.s.

$$
\operatorname{conn}\left(\mathcal{N}\left(\distgraph[n,\varepsilon]\right)\right)=d-1.
$$

Consequently, a.a.s.

$$
\chi\left(\distgraph[n,\varepsilon]\right)=d+2.
$$

This proposes a higher-dimensional extension of the preceding two-dimensional connectivity result near $\alpha=\pi$. Its status is unresolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Francisco Martinez-Figueroa, “Topology and chromatic number of random ε-distance graphs on spheres”, arXiv:2207.13892 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.13892

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

record.title: Finite-difference sign conjecture for the broken $k$-diamond partition function
record.statement:
Let $\Delta_k(n)$ be the number of the $k$-diamond broken partition of $n$, and let $D$ denote the difference operator with respect to $n$.

**Finite-difference sign conjecture.** For any $k\geq 1$ and $r\geq 1$, there exists a positive integer $n_k(r)$ such that, for $n\geq n_k(r)$,

$$
(-1)^{r-1}D^r\log \Delta_k(n)>0.
$$

This extends the proved cases for $k=1,2$ and third differences, and is analogous to the positivity of finite differences of the logarithm of the partition function. The general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Dennis X. Q. Jia, “Inequalities for the Broken k-Diamond Partition Function”, arXiv:2209.07056 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.07056

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2022). “This is analogous to the positivity of finite differences of the logarithm of the partition function, which has been proved by Chen, Wang and Xie.”

record.title: Large sparse hypergraphs are lambda-perfect conjecture
record.statement: Let $r\geq 3$. An $r$-graph $G$ has $m$ edges and is **lambda-perfect** when its Lagrangian density equals the natural complete-hypergraph lower bound determined by its number of vertices. **Sparse lambda-perfectness conjecture.** There exists $m_0$ such that for an $r$-graph $G$ with $m\geq m_0$ edges, if the number of vertices in $G$ is at least $m(r-1)+1$, then $G$ is lambda-perfect. The source presents this as a conjecture supported by several preceding theorems, but supplies no resolution.
record.source_name: Zilong Yan and Yuejian Peng, “Lagrangian densities of some 3-uniform hypergraphs”, arXiv:2209.13250 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.13250

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2022). “This conjecture was recently disproved by Baber and Talbot , and Pikhurko independently by showing that a family of several r-graphs has irrational Tur\'an density.”

record.title: The generalized approximate union-closed sets conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k\geq2$ be an integer, let $\psi_k$ be the unique real root of $(1-x)^k-x$ in $[0,1]$, and let $\mathcal F\subseteq2^{[n]}$ be a nontrivial $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximate $k$-union-closed set system, with $0\leq\varepsilon<\frac12$. Define

$$
\delta=\left(k\varepsilon+\frac{2\varepsilon\log(1/\varepsilon)}{\log|\mathcal F|}\right)^{1/(k-1)}.
$$

**Generalized approximate union-closed sets conjecture.** There is an element contained in a $\psi_k-\delta$ fraction of the sets in $\mathcal F$.
For $k=2$, this specializes to the first part of Chase and Lovett's theorem. The paper presents the assertion as an extension to almost $k$-union-closed systems; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Raphael Yuster, “Almost k-union closed set systems”, arXiv:2302.12276 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.12276

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2023). “As mentioned earlier, this was proved shortly after by several researchers.”

record.title: Hyde's conjecture on valid edge-colourings of bounded-density graphs
record.statement:
Let $H_1$ and $H_2$ be non-empty graphs with $H_1\neq H_2$ and $m_2(H_1)\geq m_2(H_2)>1$. Assume that $H_2$ is strictly $2$-balanced. If $m_2(H_1)>m_2(H_2)$, assume that $H_1$ is strictly balanced with respect to $d_2(\cdot,H_2)$; if $m_2(H_1)=m_2(H_2)$, assume that $H_1$ is strictly $2$-balanced. Let $\mathcal C(H_1,H_2)$ and $\mathcal C^*(H_1,H_2)$ be the previously defined graph classes, and for a fixed $\varepsilon>0$ define

$$
\widehat{\mathcal A}:=
\begin{cases}
\{A\in\mathcal C^*(H_1,H_2):m(A)\leq m_2(H_1,H_2)+\varepsilon\text{ and $A$ is $2$-connected}\},&m_2(H_1)>m_2(H_2),\\
\{A\in\mathcal C(H_1,H_2):m(A)\leq m_2(H_1,H_2)+\varepsilon\text{ and $A$ is $2$-connected}\},&m_2(H_1)=m_2(H_2).
\end{cases}
$$

Here a valid edge-colouring for $H_1$ and $H_2$ means the previously defined colouring notion. **Hyde's conjecture.** There exists a constant $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(H_1,H_2)>0$ such that $\widehat{\mathcal A}$ is finite and every graph in $\widehat{\mathcal A}$ has a valid edge-colouring for $H_1$ and $H_2$. The conjecture is used as a structural colouring assertion in the study of asymmetric random Ramsey thresholds, but the supplied text does not indicate that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Candida Bowtell, Robert Hancock and Joseph Hyde, “Proof of the Kohayakawa–Kreuter conjecture for the majority of cases”, arXiv:2307.16760 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.16760

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

record.title: The bridgeless-intersection extremal conjecture
record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of graphs on $[n]$. Say that a graph is **2-edge-connected** when it is connected and bridgeless.

**Bridgeless-intersection conjecture.** If the intersection of any two graphs in $\mathcal{F}$ is 2-edge-connected, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq \frac{1}{2^n}\cdot 2^{\binom{n}{2}}.
$$

The natural expected extremal family consists of all graphs containing a fixed $n$-cycle, but the authors state that they have been unable to prove this bound.
record.source_name: Imre Leader, Žarko Ranđelović and Ta Sheng Tan, “A Note on Hamiltonian-Intersecting Families of Graphs”, arXiv:2309.00757 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00757

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

record.title: Cyclic cube-free density conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{Z}_N$ be the cyclic group of order $N$, and let $A\subset\mathbb{Z}_N$ be **$d$-cube-free**, meaning that there is no multiset $S=\{a_1,\ldots,a_d\}$ such that

$$
\Sigma^*S=\left\{\sum_{i\in I}a_i:\varnothing\neq I\subset [d]\right\}\subset A.
$$

**Cyclic cube-free density conjecture.** If $d\mid N$, then

$$
|A|\leqslant \frac{d-1}{d}N.
$$

The bound is sharp: when $N$ is divisible by $d$, the set $\{b\in\mathbb{Z}_N:b\equiv 1,2,\ldots,d-1\pmod d\}$ has this size. The paper proves the case $d=3$, while the general assertion remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Yuchen Meng, “A note on cube-free problems”, arXiv:2311.12318 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12318

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

record.title: Archdeacon's existence conjecture for integer Heffter arrays
record.statement:
Let $m,n,s,k$ be integers such that $3\leqslant s\leqslant n$, $3\leqslant k\leqslant m$, and $ms=nk$. An **integer Heffter array** $\mathrm{H}(m,n;s,k)$ is an $m\times n$ partially filled array with $s$ filled cells in each row and $k$ filled cells in each column, whose entries use one representative from each pair $\{x,-x\}$ partitioning $\{1,2,\ldots,2nk+1\}$, and whose rows and columns each sum to zero.

**Archdeacon's conjecture.** There exists an integer Heffter array $\mathrm{H}(m,n;s,k)$ if and only if

$$
nk\equiv 0,3\pmod 4.
$$

This conjecture gives the expected necessary and sufficient arithmetic condition for the existence of integer Heffter arrays with at least three filled cells in every row and column. The source presents it as an established conjecture in the literature; its resolution is not specified here.
record.source_name: Fiorenza Morini and Marco Antonio Pellegrini, “Signed magic arrays: existence and constructions”, arXiv:2410.04101 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2407.15183](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.15183).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.04101

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

record.title: Kronenthal–Lazebnik's uniqueness conjecture for generalized quadrangles over algebraically closed fields
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $f_2,f_3\in\mathbb F[p_1,l_1]$. **Kronenthal–Lazebnik's conjecture.** Every graph $B\Gamma_3(\mathbb F;f_2,f_3)$ with girth at least eight is isomorphic to

$$
B\Gamma_3(\mathbb F;p_1l_1,p_1l_1^2).
$$

The claim would establish uniqueness of this generalized-quadrangle construction over algebraically closed fields; the source presents it as expected and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Felix Lazebnik and Ye Wang, “Some families of graphs, hypergraphs and digraphs defined by systems of equations”, arXiv:2503.07915 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07915

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: Lazebnik–Ustimenko–Woldar's diameter upper-bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $C\!D(k,q)$ be a connected component of $D(k,q)$, with $k\ge 2$ and $q$ a prime power. **Lazebnik–Ustimenko–Woldar's conjecture.** There is a positive constant $C$ such that

$$
\operatorname{diam}(C\!D(k,q))\le (\log_{q-1}q)k+C.
$$

This predicts a linear diameter bound with coefficient $\log_{q-1}q$; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Felix Lazebnik and Ye Wang, “Some families of graphs, hypergraphs and digraphs defined by systems of equations”, arXiv:2503.07915 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07915

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: Characterization of zero uniform Turán density for r-graphs
record.statement:
Let $F$ be an $r$-graph. An ordering $\preceq$ on $V(F)$ and a function

$$
\varphi:\binom{V(F)}{2}\rightarrow\binom{[r]}{2}
$$

assign to each pair of vertices the role it plays in an edge containing that pair. The **zero-density characterization conjecture.**

$$
\pi_{\!\text{uniform}}(F)=0
$$

if and only if there exists an ordering $\preceq$ on $V(F)$ and such a function $\varphi$ with the property that, for each pair of vertices $u,v$ and every edge $e$ containing $u$ and $v$, the pair $\{u,v\}$ plays the role $\varphi(uv)$ in $e$.

For $3$-graphs, Reiher, Rödl and Schacht proved the analogous characterization. Extending it to $r$-graphs for general $r$ would characterize exactly the forbidden hypergraphs of zero uniform Turán density; the general case is left open in the source.
record.source_name: Ander Lamaison, “Uniform Turán density beyond 3-graphs”, arXiv:2508.20696 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20696

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).

record.title: Doumas–Papanicolaou's finite variance-minimization conjecture for the double Dixie cup problem
record.statement:
Let $m$ and $N$ be fixed, let $p$ range over the probability simplex on $N$ coupon types, and let $T_m(N)$ denote the number of draws needed to collect at least $m$ copies of every type. For a probability vector $p$, write $\operatorname{Var}_p(T_m(N))$ for the variance under the corresponding coupon-collection process, and let

$$
u=(1/N,\ldots,1/N).
$$

**Finite variance extremality.** The equal-probability vector $\nu$ minimizes

$$
p\mapsto \operatorname{Var}_p(T_m(N))
$$

over the probability simplex.
The conjecture concerns variance minimization in the nonuniform double Dixie cup problem. Its $m=1$ case was later proved by Yu, while the statement for general fixed $m$ remains unresolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Christopher D. Long, “Terminal Defects, Growing Multiplicity, and Variance Extremality in the Double Dixie Cup Problem”, arXiv:2604.25108 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25108

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2026).

record.title: Andrews–Bachraoui conjecture on the signed generating function for $a_2(n)$
record.statement:
Let $a_2”(n)$ be the signed count of the partitions described above, with each partition having $j$ parts greater than $1$ assigned weight $(-1)^{j+1}$. Define

$$
\chi(n)=\begin{cases}-1&\text{if }n\equiv 0,1\pmod 4,\\1&\text{if }n\equiv 2,3\pmod 4.\end{cases}
$$

**Andrews–Bachraoui conjecture.** There holds

$$
\sum_{n\geq 0}a_2”(n)q^n=\frac{q}{1-q^2}+\frac{1}{1+q}\sum_{n\geq 0}\chi(n)q^{\binom{n+1}{2}+1}.
$$

This conjecture was stated in the earlier paper cited in the source and concerns an unexpectedly simple expression for the signed generating function. No resolution is supplied in the given text.
record.source_name: George E. Andrews, Mohamed El Bachraoui, Aritram Dhar, Ankush Goswami and Runqiao Li, “Weighted partitions with interval restrictions: exact formulas and a bivariate master identity”, arXiv:2606.11011 (2026).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2604.05403](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05403), [arXiv:2604.02239](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02239).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11011

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

record.title: Perfect-power square-maximality conjecture for induced grid subgraphs
record.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and $n\ge1$. If $S\subset\mathbb{Z}^d$ has $|S|=n^d$ and the induced graph $\mathcal L_d[S]$ is connected, then

$$
\tau(\mathcal L_d[S])\le \tau(P_n^{\square d}).
$$

**Perfect-power square-maximality conjecture.** Equality should occur only for the $d$-dimensional box $P_n^{\square d}$, up to lattice translation and coordinate permutation.

For $d=2$, this specializes to the square-maximality conjecture attributed to Procaccia and Tucker-Foltz. For non-perfect-power vertex counts, the expected maximizing induced grid subgraph may be a compact near-box shape rather than a product, so exact maximality remains open beyond the stated perfect-power case.
record.source_name: Jiechen Zhang, “Extremal Spanning Trees in Product Grid Graphs”, arXiv:2606.24016 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24016

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

record.title: Nearest-neighbor critical-radius conjecture for the square-lattice disc model
record.statement:
Let $R_c^{\texttt{NN}}(p)$ denote the critical radius for the nearest-neighbor model with parameter $p$, and let $R_c^{\texttt{dec}}$ denote the critical radius of the decorrelated model. **Critical-radius conjecture.**

$$
R_c^{\texttt{NN}}(\infty)=R_c^{\texttt{dec}}=1.
$$

Numerical simulations suggest this equality. At $R=1$, the nearest-neighbor model has edge density $1/2$, matching the critical probability for Bernoulli percolation on the square lattice, while the decorrelated model has a symmetry around $R=1$. The exact critical radii remain to be determined.
record.source_name: Jérôme Casse, Irène Marcovici and Maxence Poutrel, “Gilbert's disc model conditioned on the square lattice”, arXiv:2607.14062 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14062

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).
